_doc: Source data for /wealth/. One record per fund. Every figure carries its source, date and basis. basis: official | official_converted (official local-currency figure converted at the stated official rate) | estimate (third party).

ranking.source: Global SWF ranking (October 2026), entries classed as sovereign wealth funds (type SWF), by AuM

funds.name: Government Pension Fund Global (Norway)
funds.blurb: Norway's oil fund, managed by NBIM for the Ministry of Finance. It owns shares in about 7,100 listed companies.

source.name: NBIM, key figures Q3 2026
source.locator: "The fund was valued at 22,014 billion kroner on 30 September 2026"

fx.source: ECB euro reference rates (USD 1.1355 and NOK 10.9015 per EUR)

source.name: NBIM, key figures Q3 2026
source.locator: Share of fund by asset class

alloc.note: Shares of the fund's value as published by NBIM. NBIM also publishes every individual holding.

regions.title: Equity portfolio by region

source.name: NBIM, half-year report 2026

regions.note: As published: the shares add to 100.5% because the half-year report footnote says cash and derivatives are not included.

source.name: NBIM, fund page: largest equity holdings

holdings.note: NBIM publishes every holding, twice a year; the ten largest equity positions are shown.

notes: NBIM's half-year report names the fund's three largest government bond holdings as US, Japanese and German bonds (30 June 2026).
funds.other_funds: Norway also has the Government Pension Fund Norway (managed by Folketrygdfondet), a separate, much smaller fund.

funds.name: SAFE Investment Company (China)
funds.manager: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), through SAFE Investment Company
funds.blurb: The investment arm that manages part of China's foreign exchange reserves. It publishes neither its assets nor its allocation.

source.name: Global SWF, Ranking of sovereign and public pension funds (October 2026)

assets.estimate_note: SAFE IC does not publish its total assets. This is Global SWF's estimate, not an official figure.

pop.source: National Bureau of Statistics of China, 2025 statistical communique
pop.scope: Mainland China: 31 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities plus servicemen; excludes Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan and foreigners

notes: SAFE publishes China's official foreign exchange reserves, but not how much of them SAFE IC manages or what it holds.
funds.other_funds: China has two large sovereign funds on this list: SAFE IC and China Investment Corporation (CIC).

funds.name: China Investment Corporation
funds.blurb: China's sovereign wealth fund. It runs an overseas portfolio and, through Central Huijin, holds state stakes in China's big banks and financial firms.

source.name: CIC Annual Report 2024, consolidated balance sheet
source.locator: Total Assets US$1,567,334 million; net assets US$1.37 trillion

assets.note: Total assets of the CIC group, which includes Central Huijin's domestic financial holdings (long-term equity investments US$967.8 billion), not only the overseas portfolio. The 2025 annual report is not yet out.

pop.source: National Bureau of Statistics of China, 2025 statistical communique
pop.scope: Mainland China: 31 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities plus servicemen; excludes Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan and foreigners

alloc.title: Overseas (global investment) portfolio

source.name: CIC Annual Report 2024

rows.name: Alternative assets (hedge funds, private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, resources)

alloc.note: Covers the overseas investment portfolio only. CIC does not split the alternatives line into private equity, real estate and the rest.

notes: Ten-year annualised net return on overseas investments: 6.92% in US dollars (CIC Annual Report 2024).
Central Huijin, a CIC subsidiary, manages state-owned financial capital of CNY 6.87 trillion (end-2024).
funds.other_funds: China has two large sovereign funds on this list: SAFE IC and China Investment Corporation (CIC).

funds.name: GIC (Singapore)
funds.blurb: Singapore's fund that manages the government's reserves. It publishes returns and a three-group asset mix, but not its total assets.

source.name: Global SWF, Ranking of sovereign and public pension funds (October 2026)

assets.estimate_note: GIC does not publish the size of the portfolio. This is Global SWF's estimate, not an official figure.

pop.source: Singapore Department of Statistics, Population Trends 2026
pop.scope: Total population incl. non-residents (1.98 million); citizens 3,684,888

source.name: GIC, Report on the Management of the Government's Portfolio 2025/26

rows.name: Real assets (real estate, infrastructure and other)

alloc.note: GIC reports three broad asset groups that cover both public and private markets. It does not publish separate weights for bonds, real estate or private equity.

source.name: GIC, Report on the Management of the Government's Portfolio 2025/26

rows.name: Global (funds, commodities and supranational debt without geographic detail)

notes: Annualised 20-year real return to 31 March 2026: 3.4% above global inflation (5.6% nominal, in US dollars).
funds.other_funds: Singapore's other large sovereign fund is Temasek.

funds.name: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority
funds.blurb: Abu Dhabi's largest fund. It does not publish its assets; it publishes allocation ranges and long-term returns.

source.name: Global SWF, Ranking of sovereign and public pension funds (October 2026)

assets.estimate_note: ADIA does not disclose its assets under management. This is Global SWF's estimate, not an official figure.

pop.source: IMF World Economic Outlook, October 2026 (population estimate)
pop.scope: UAE total population (includes the large expatriate population)

alloc.title: Long-term strategy portfolio: allocation ranges

source.name: ADIA 2025 Review
source.locator: Long-Term Strategy Portfolio: Portfolio by Asset Class

alloc.note: These are target ranges within which allocations can move, not actual weights, so they do not add to 100%. ADIA does not publish its actual allocation.

source.name: ADIA 2025 Review
source.locator: Long-Term Strategy Portfolio: Portfolio by Geography

notes: Annualised returns in US dollars: 6.6% over 20 years and 7.2% over 30 years (ADIA 2025 Review).
funds.other_funds: The UAE has several large sovereign funds, including Abu Dhabi's ADIA, Mubadala and L'imad, and Dubai's ICD.

funds.name: Kuwait Investment Authority
funds.blurb: Kuwait's fund manages the General Reserve Fund and the Future Generations Fund. It does not publish its assets or allocation.

source.name: Global SWF, Ranking of sovereign and public pension funds (October 2026)

assets.estimate_note: KIA does not publish its assets or allocation. This is Global SWF's estimate, not an official figure.

pop.source: IMF World Economic Outlook, October 2026 (population estimate)

funds.name: Public Investment Fund (Saudi Arabia)
funds.blurb: Saudi Arabia's sovereign fund, which funds the Vision 2030 projects. About three-quarters of its assets are invested inside the Kingdom.

source.name: PIF Annual Report 2025, gross assets under management

fx.source: Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) peg: 3.75 riyals per US dollar

assets.note: Gross assets under management, which PIF says include SAR 30 billion of receivables from other parties. PIF's balance-sheet total assets differ (consolidated total assets SAR 3,166.5 billion at end-2025).

pop.source: General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT), Population Estimates 2024
pop.scope: Total population: 19.6 million Saudis and 15.7 million non-Saudis (latest official estimate is mid-2024)

alloc.title: By investment pool

source.name: PIF Annual Report 2025
source.locator: Performance Review, gross AuM by pool

rows.name: Saudi Real Estate and Infrastructure Development

alloc.note: PIF reports by investment pool, not by asset class (equities, bonds and so on). Percentages are as published and may not add to 100% because of rounding. The pools shown add to SAR 3,367 billion, SAR 29 billion less than the total; PIF's footnote says its AuM includes SAR 30 billion of receivables from other parties.

source.name: PIF Annual Report 2025

sectors.title: By sector (GICS)

source.name: PIF Annual Report 2025
source.locator: Performance Review, PIF investments by sector

rows.name: Unclassified (multisector funds, cash and money markets)

sectors.note: Shares are as published and may not add to 100% because of rounding.

notes: Average annual total portfolio return of 5.8% since the Vision Realization Program launched in 2017, to December 31, 2025 (PIF Annual Report 2025).

funds.name: Qatar Investment Authority
funds.blurb: Qatar's sovereign fund, funded by gas revenue. It does not publish its assets or allocation.

source.name: Global SWF, Ranking of sovereign and public pension funds (October 2026)

assets.estimate_note: QIA does not publish its assets or allocation. This is Global SWF's estimate, not an official figure.

pop.source: IMF World Economic Outlook, October 2026 (population estimate)

funds.name: Türkiye Wealth Fund
funds.blurb: Türkiye's state holding fund. It consolidates large state companies and banks, so its balance sheet is that of a group.

source.name: TWF consolidated statement of financial position, 31 December 2025 (audited)

fx.source: ECB euro reference rates (USD 1.175 and TRY 50.4838 per EUR)

assets.note: Consolidated total assets of the fund and its subsidiaries, including the balance sheets of banks it owns, so it is larger than the value of its equity stakes.

pop.source: TurkStat, Address Based Population Registration System results 2025 (bulletin of 9 Feb 2026)
pop.scope: Resident population at 31 December 2025, as published in TurkStat's bulletin of 9 February 2026 (also reported by Anadolu Agency)

notes: The fund does not publish an asset-class mix; its accounts consolidate its subsidiaries instead.
